draft.title: Reflection statements
card: A reflection statement is a short piece in which a writer explains the choices they made in their own writing. It says what they did and why.
It links those choices to a purpose, an audience or a studied text. For example, a writer might say they used short sentences to build tension, as the author of a text they studied did.
It discusses craft: structure, voice, language techniques and their effects on a reader. It names a technique, shows where it was used and explains its effect.
It does not retell the plot of the piece or describe how hard or how long the work was. Comments such as "I worked hard on this" do not explain a choice.
draft.remember: A reflection explains craft choices and the reasons for them, not the effort.

a.q: Which sentence would best belong in a reflection statement?
opts: I ended with a question to leave the reader unsettled
I spent many hours on this story over three weeks
My story is about a girl who moves to a new town
I found the task difficult but I kept trying to finish
a.why: The first sentence names a choice and gives its effect on the reader. The sentence about hours spent describes effort, not craft, so it explains no choice.
a.clue: Which sentence explains a choice and its effect?

b.q: Priya wrote a short story about a lonely night shift. Which part of her reflection best meets the purpose of a reflection statement?
opts: I used a cold, bare setting, as in our studied text, to show isolation
I wrote four drafts and stayed up late to fix the ending
The story follows a nurse who finds a lost child in the ward
I chose this topic because I enjoy writing about hospitals
b.why: The first option names a choice, links it to a studied text and explains its purpose. The draft count is tempting because it shows commitment, but it describes effort, not craft.
b.clue: Look for a choice, a reason and a link to a studied text.
